description:
The BIG-IP ASM, F5 Advanced Web Application Firewall (Advanced WAF), and NGINX App Protect systems may fail to detect encoded directory traversal in the URL. This issue occurs when the following condition is met:

The affected security policy is enabled with an evasion technique detected violation (enabled by default). For more information about this violation on BIG-IP ASM and Advanced WAF, refer to K7929: Working with evasion technique detected violations. For more information about this violation on NGINX App Protect, refer to the NGINX App Protect WAF Configuration Guide.
impact:
An attacker is able to bypass BIG-IP ASM, Advanced WAF, and NGINX App Protect system detection when performing a URL-encoded directory traversal attack.

Symptoms

As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom:

The back-end server receives requests that should have been blocked by the BIG-IP ASM, Advanced WAF, and NGINX App Protect systems.
mitigation:
To mitigate this issue, you should assign the following attack signatures to the affected security policy.

Impact of action: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system.

Signature ID	Name	Attack Type / Signature Set	Last Updated
200007033	Directory Traversal attempt "../" (URI) (%2e.)	Path Traversal	2020/12/28
200007034	Directory Traversal attempt "../" (URI) (.%2e)	Path Traversal	2020/12/28
200007035	Directory Traversal attempt "../" (URI) (%2e%2e)	Path Traversal	2020/12/28

You can either create a custom signature set that includes these attack signatures or use the Path Traversal Attack Signature Set, which includes these attack signatures, by default. You should then assign either the custom signature set or the Path Traversal Attack Signature Set to the affected security policy. For information about creating a custom signature set, as well as assigning a signature set to a security policy, refer to the Assigning Attack Signatures to Security Policies chapter of the BIG-IP Application Security Manager: Attack and Bot Signatures manual. Note: For information about how to locate F5 product guides, refer to K98133564: Tips for searching AskF5 and finding product documentation.

For information about configuring attack signatures on NGINX App Protect, refer to the Configuring Attack Signatures section of the NGINX App Protect WAF Configuration Guide.
recommended_actions:
If you are running a version listed in the Versions affected by this issue column, you can eliminate this issue by installing a version listed in the Fixes introduced in column. If the Fixes introduced in column does not list a version for your branch, then no update candidate currently exists for that branch and F5 recommends upgrading to a version with the fix (refer to the table).

If the Fixes introduced in column lists a version prior to the one you are running, in the same branch, then your version should have the fix.
title: K70134152: BIG-IP ASM, F5 Advanced WAF, and NGINX App Protect encoded directory traversal security exposure
